studies.label: Between-subjects food-waste brainstorming experiment: human + GLM versus human-only

arms.name: human + GLM
arms.description: Individual brainstorming in the purpose-built app with its GLM function active. Participants request suggestions using a fixed-prompt Generate ideas button and may copy, edit, or ignore them; at least one request was required (PDF pp. 9-10, printed pp. 1031-1032, Sects. 3.2-3.3).

arms.name: human-only
arms.description: Individual brainstorming in the same app with its GLM function deactivated (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1031, Sect. 3.2).

studies.task: Brainstorm for 10 minutes on “How can we reduce food waste?”, then select the four best ideas from the long list (PDF p. 8, printed p. 1030, Sect. 3.1; PDF p. 11, printed p. 1033, Sect. 3.5).

ai_tool.name: OpenAI GPT-3.5-turbo-0301 (temperature 0.9), embedded in the brainstorming app
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 1031), Sect. 3.3; model and temperature explicitly named, model release year not stated

studies.shared_sample: The reconciled screening form flags possible overlap with Memmert and Bittner (2024; c861) and a related ECIS report based on matching participant quotations. The present paper makes no explicit overlap statement. Quantitative participant overlap and sample independence remain unconfirmed.

open_items: The paper does not print the number randomized or labeled per-arm analyzed counts. Sect. 3.4 (PDF p. 10, printed p. 1032) reports 77 completers and two exclusions, leaving 75; Sect. 3.6 (PDF p. 12, printed p. 1034) mentions group sizes of 38 and 37 without identifying the arms. No arm count was inferred. The four further exclusions from the human-judge human-level shortlist ratings have no printed final analysis total; GPT-4 robustness analysis counts and exclusion handling are not separately stated.

Participant-level arm SDs, SEs, and numerical confidence limits are absent. Only human-judge dyad novelty has printed arm means. The interval type and endpoints in Fig. 8c (PDF p. 13, printed p. 1035) are not stated; no statistics were digitized or derived.
Human-fluency significance conflicts: Sect. 4.1 prints p = 0.015, while Fig. 7a uses ** with caption **p < .01 (PDF pp. 12-13, printed pp. 1034-1035). The text value is retained.

For human fluency the paper prints a negative rank-biserial correlation but a positive converted Cohen’s d; no conversion formula or SD denominator is specified. The standardizer for the human-judge dyad novelty Cohen’s d is also not defined (PDF pp. 12-13, printed pp. 1034-1035).

The Good-Idea-Count novelty threshold is printed as 3.396 in Sect. 4.1 and the same number is printed as the treated dyad-level human-judge novelty mean in Sect. 4.2 (PDF p. 13, printed p. 1035). Online Appendix D may clarify whether this is intentional; no correction was made.

Online Appendices A-E are outside the saved PDF and no matching local supplement was found. On 2026-10-10, urllib requests with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 to https://media.springernature.com/full/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1007%2Fs12599-025-00974-y/MediaObjects/12599_2025_974_MOESM1_ESM.pdf and then https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12599-025-00974-y both failed with WinError 10013. Supplement contents remain unverified.

The screening form flags possible participant overlap with c861 and a related ECIS paper; the present paper does not establish the overlapping participants. Independent sample IDs require reconciliation.
The paper does not designate human-level or dyad-level novelty as primary and reports no preregistration. Selection between the two human-judge novelty records remains an Atlas decision.

The experiment took place in university seminars; whether the task was ordinary coursework and explicitly supervised is not stated. lab_rct follows the standardized experimental task and the reconciled form. Only a Western European university is specified for the participants, so no country was inferred from author affiliations.
